description: Ivanakbar Purwamaska and Patrick Fulton at Cornell University publish numerical sensitivity tests for estimating subsurface permeability from borehole thermal recovery. The September 2026 version-two release contains temperature-time outputs and spatial residual-temperature grids, free under CC BY 4.0. Its README documents permeability from 10^-12 to 10^-20 square metres, depth from 50 to 750 metres, formation thickness from 0.5 to 10 metres, circulation duration from two to twelve hours, and imposed circulation pressure from 250 to 3,000 kilopascals. This pressure is an experimental boundary condition, not total in situ pressure. These results can benchmark hydrothermal inference used in geothermal and groundwater simulations. The same-family 2025 release includes a representative COMSOL base model and MATLAB analysis, but the exact version-two COMSOL model is unavailable. No related catalogue record explicitly covers the family. Reproducibility and parameter uncertainty remain limited by that missing configuration; no numerical files or software were tested.
